g1.label: 1. Paths form where the official route is longer
g1.why: Paragraph A: they “usually appear where an official path makes walkers go … the long way round”.

g2.label: 2. Takes several years to form
g2.why: Paragraph A says they “can form in a single season” — the opposite of several years.

g3.label: 3. More common in cities than the countryside
g3.why: The text only talks about city parks and campuses; it never compares them with the countryside.

g4.label: 4. Fences and signs always worked
g4.why: Paragraph B says these measures “sometimes worked” — “always” contradicts that.

g5.label: 5. Most managers now encourage walking on grass
g5.why: Paragraph C is about “a growing number of designers”, not most park managers, and says nothing about encouraging people.

g6.label: 6. Supporters say the resulting paths get used
g6.why: Paragraph C: supporters say it “produces paths that people use instead of ignore”.

g7.label: 7. May not suit every walker
g7.why: Paragraph D: a route that suits commuters “may not suit wheelchair users or parents with buggies”.

g1.label: 1. usually closed → never closed
g1.why: “Never closed” contradicts “usually closed”, so the statement is False.

g2.label: 2. free on Sundays → free every day
g2.why: The text says nothing about the other six days, so it neither confirms nor contradicts “every day”.

g3.label: 3. still unsure → have proved
g3.why: If scientists are still unsure, they have not proved it — the statement contradicts the text.

g4.label: 4. most arrive by train → more than any other
g4.why: “Most” means more than half, so train must be the biggest group — the statement agrees.

g5.label: 5. only a few survive → some still standing
g5.why: “A few survive” means some are still standing, even though most are gone.

g6.label: 6. first held in 1998 → every year since
g6.why: The text gives the first year only; it does not say whether the festival was held every year after that.

g7.label: 7. almost all grow rice → rice is the only crop
g7.why: Farmers can grow rice and other crops too; the text does not say what else is grown.

g8.label: 8. more than 50 employees → 20 employees
g8.why: A company with 20 employees is below the limit of 50, so the law does not apply — False.

g1.correct: a quicker way to get somewhere
accept: a quicker way to get somewhere
g1.label: 1. a shortcut
g1.why: A shortcut is a route that is quicker or shorter than the usual one.

g2.correct: the actions taken to deal with the problem
accept: the actions taken to deal with the problem
g2.label: 2. these measures
g2.why: “Measures” here are actions taken to solve a problem — the fences, hedges and signs.

g3.label: 3. a growing number of
g3.why: If a number is growing, it is getting bigger: more and more designers.

g4.label: 4. free information
g4.why: The paths show how people move without anyone paying for a study — the information costs nothing.

g5.label: 5. reflect
g5.why: Here “reflect” means show or represent — the paths show how one group of people walks.

g6.label: 6. hurried
g6.why: Hurried people are in a rush, so they take the quickest route.

g7.label: 7. consensus (IELTS Vocabulary Glossary)
g7.why: A consensus is general agreement — a word from the IELTS Vocabulary Glossary.

g8.label: 8. undermine (IELTS Vocabulary Glossary)
g8.why: To undermine something is to make it weaker, often slowly — from the IELTS Vocabulary Glossary.
